rename_teach.M1.S4.T4.C12: What to Measure: three arms from a point
rename_teach.M4.S15.T15.C48: Rules at Work: the missing angles

into.name: What to Measure: the two V-shaped figures
into.q_figure: Two V-shaped figures side by side, each made of a short arm and a long arm meeting at an elbow, with no measurements written on them.
into.s_figure: The two V-shaped figures with the short arm, the long arm and the elbow angle of each marked so that the two elbow angles can be compared.

into.name: What to Measure: which pairs are congruent
into.q_figure: Four pairs of figures: two teardrops, two clouds, two starbursts and two pairs of leaf shapes, with nothing written on them.
into.s_figure: The same four pairs with the congruent pairs circled.

into.name: What to Measure: copying a circle and a rectangle
into.s_figure: A circle with its radius drawn and labelled, and a rectangle with its length and breadth labelled.

questions.q_figure: One figure of three straight arms meeting at a point, one pointing up and to the left and two running in opposite directions along a slanted line, shown once on its own and then as two pairs of such figures, with no lengths or angles written.
questions.s_figure: One figure of three arms with the three arm lengths and two of the angles between the arms marked.

questions.name: Writing the Match: a pair in the rectangle
questions.q_figure: A rectangle ABCD with A at the top left, B at the top right, C at the bottom right and D at the bottom left, and the diagonal BD drawn.
questions.s_figure: The two triangles ABD and CDB drawn apart, with the equal sides AB and CD marked alike, AD and CB marked alike, and the shared side BD marked.

questions.name: Writing the Match: the right correspondence
questions.q_figure: A rectangle ABCD cut along the diagonal BD into triangles ABD and CDB, beside a two-column table that pairs A with C, B with B and D with D.
questions.s_figure: The triangles ABD and CDB drawn apart with the corresponding vertices joined by lines: A to C, B to D and D to B.

questions.name: Writing the Match: HEN and BIG
questions.s_figure: The statement triangle HEN congruent to triangle BIG written out, with each shuffled version listed beneath it.

questions.name: Two Triangles Apart: the kite ABCD
questions.q_figure: A four-sided figure ABCD with A at the top, B at the lower left, C at the bottom and D at the right, with AB and AD marked with one tick each, CB and CD marked with two ticks each, and a dashed line from A to C.
questions.s_figure: The two triangles ABC and ADC drawn apart, with the equal sides marked alike and the shared side AC marked.

into.name: Two Triangles Apart: RED and JAM
into.q_figure: Two triangles: RED with R at the top left, E at the bottom left and D at the bottom right, RE = 3.5 cm, ED = 5 cm and DR = 6 cm; and JAM with J at the left, A at the bottom right and M at the top right, JA = 3.5 cm, AM = 5 cm and MJ = 6 cm.
into.s_figure: The two triangles with the equal sides marked in matching colours and the corners R, E, D matched with J, A, M.

into.name: Two Triangles Apart: the arrowhead
into.q_figure: An arrowhead figure with D at the top, F at the bottom left, G at the bottom right and E on the line below D, with DF and DG marked with one tick each, FE and GE marked with two ticks each, and DE drawn.
into.s_figure: The two triangles DFE and DGE drawn apart, with the equal sides marked alike and the shared side DE marked.

questions.name: Two Angles and a Side: the midpoint figure
questions.q_figure: Two segments AD and BC crossing at O, with A at the top left, C at the top right, B at the bottom left and D at the bottom right, AB and CD joined, AO and OD marked with one tick each and BO and OC marked with two ticks each.
questions.s_figure: The two triangles AOB and DOC drawn apart, with the equal sides AO and OD and BO and OC marked and the angles at O marked.

into.name: Two Angles and a Side: the 47 degree pair
into.q_figure: Two triangles: ABC with A at the top, B at the bottom left and C at the bottom right, AB = 7 cm, BC = 5 cm and the angle at B equal to 47 degrees; and XYZ with X at the top left, Y at the bottom and Z at the right, XZ = 7 cm, YZ = 5 cm and the angle at Z equal to 47 degrees.
into.s_figure: The two triangles with the 47 degree angles and the 7 cm and 5 cm sides around them marked, and the corners B, A, C matched with Z, X, Y.

into.name: Two Angles and a Side: parallel lines AB and CD
into.q_figure: Segments DB and AC crossing at O, with D at the top left, C at the top right, A at the bottom left and B at the bottom right, DC and AB joined, drawn with parallel arrows and marked equal in length.
into.s_figure: The triangles COD and AOB drawn apart, with the equal alternate angles at C and A and at D and B marked and the equal sides DC and AB marked.

into.name: Two Angles and a Side: the shared side BC
into.q_figure: A four-sided figure with A at the top, B at the left, C at the right and D at the bottom, the line BC drawn across the middle, angles ABC and DBC marked with one arc each and angles ACB and DCB marked with two arcs each.
into.s_figure: The triangles ABC and DBC drawn apart, sharing the side BC, with the equal angles at B and at C marked.

into.name: Two Angles and a Side: crossing lines AC and DB
into.q_figure: Segments AC and DB crossing at O, with A at the top left, D at the top right, B at the bottom left and C at the bottom right, AB, DC and BC drawn, angles ABD and DCA marked with one arc each and angles ACB and DBC marked with two arcs each.
into.s_figure: The triangles ABC and DCB drawn apart, sharing the side BC, with the equal angles at B and at C marked.

questions.name: Equal Sides: finding angles B and C
questions.q_figure: An isosceles triangle ABC with AB and AC marked with one tick each and the angle at A equal to 80 degrees.
questions.s_figure: The same triangle with the altitude from A to BC drawn and the angles at B and C each marked 50 degrees.

into.name: Rules at Work: AIR and FLY
into.s_figure: The statement triangle AIR congruent to triangle FLY written out, with arrows joining A to F, I to L and R to Y.

into.name: Rules at Work: five cases of three facts
into.q_figure: Five boxes labelled (a) to (e), each listing three facts: (a) AB = DE, BC = EF, CA = DF; (b) AB = EF, angle A = angle E, AC = ED; (c) AB = DF, angle B = angle D = 90 degrees, AC = FE; (d) angle A = angle D, angle B = angle E, AC = DF; (e) AB = DF, angle B = angle F, AC = DE.
into.s_figure: For each case a small sketch of the two triangles with the three given equal parts marked and the rule named under it.

questions.name: Rules at Work: AB parallel to CD
questions.q_figure: Segments AD and BC crossing at O, with A at the top left, C at the top right, B at the bottom left and D at the bottom right, AB and CD joined, OA and OD marked with one tick each and OB and OC marked with two ticks each.
questions.s_figure: The triangles AOB and DOC drawn apart with the equal sides and the vertically opposite angles at O marked, and the equal alternate angles OAB and ODC marked on the lines AB and CD cut by the line AD.

into.name: Rules at Work: the square ABCD
into.q_figure: A square ABCD with A at the top left, B at the top right, C at the bottom right and D at the bottom left, and the diagonal AC drawn.
into.s_figure: The square cut along the diagonal AC into triangles ABC and ADC, with the equal sides marked alike.

into.name: Rules at Work: the centre of the circle
into.q_figure: A circle with centre A, points B and C on the circle joined to A and to each other, and the angle at A marked 120 degrees.
into.s_figure: The same triangle with the angles at B and C each marked 30 degrees.

questions.q_figure: A large rectangle CDBA with C at the top left, D at the top right, B at the bottom right and A at the bottom left, crossed by many segments that join the points R and V on the top side, U on the left side, F on the right side and K and L on the bottom side to inner points, with single, double and triple tick marks on equal segments, right angle marks at C, B and L, and some angles of 34, 68, 98, 44, 46, 90, 56 and 30 degrees marked while the rest are left blank.
questions.s_figure: The same rectangle figure with the missing angle written into each triangle once it is worked out.
